proposal.rationale: Observed failures show the model concluding from incomplete search evidence. In `sanitize-git-repo`, the agent used broad recursive searches piped through `head` (`grep -RIn ... | head -200`, `find ... | xargs -0 grep ... | head -200`) and tool outputs were also truncated (`... [8035 original chars; middle omitted] ...`). It then edited only two files and missed at least one additional Hugging Face token; the verifier later reported another token still present. In `extract-elf`, the agent relied on large `readelf` outputs that were truncated (`readelf -h/-S/-l` output had an omission marker), then built an incomplete extractor that found only 0–18.5% of expected keys. This proposal differs from the rejected line-compaction attempt: it does not alter truncation strategy or summarize more aggressively, which previously regressed quality. Instead it preserves existing outputs and adds a small, targeted caution only when evidence is likely partial, nudging the model to avoid false exhaustiveness. Expected benefit: better completeness checks with minimal token/time cost. Likely regression: occasional extra follow-up command on tasks where partial output was already enough, slightly increasing duration.
proposal.hypothesis: If the agent is explicitly warned whenever a recursive search/listing command is likely incomplete because it used `head`/`tail`/`sed -n` slicing or the captured output was truncated, the model will less often treat partial evidence as exhaustive and will follow up with narrower or counted searches before editing or declaring done, improving wrong-output tasks driven by missed matches.
proposal.change_summary: Add a lightweight partial-evidence warning: when a search/listing command uses `head`/`tail`/`sed -n` or its captured output was truncated, append a note telling the model not to treat the result as exhaustive and to rerun with narrower scope/counts if completeness matters.

proposal.rationale: Observed failures share a pattern of the model producing plausible outputs without enough exact evidence. In fix-git, after a cherry-pick conflict the agent manually rewrote `_includes/about.md` with `cat > _includes/about.md <<'EOF' ...` and later the verifier reported the file hash was wrong even though the merge completed; this is direct evidence that freehand reconstruction can fail. In sqlite-db-truncate, the agent wrote `/app/recover.json` with guessed sequential values via `records=[{'word':f'testword{i:02d}','value':i} for i in range(10)]`, and the test scored `0` matches; that is strong evidence of guessing instead of decoding. In extract-elf, the agent emitted many addresses from raw file offsets, then only 40 keys, and the test reported `0.00%` expected values found; again the output was structurally valid but not derived from the right source of truth. In sanitize-git-repo, the agent replaced a few hardcoded tokens and then checked only those exact strings with `grep ... 'AKIA123...|...|hf_abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz123456'`, while the test later showed another Hugging Face token remained; this is consistent with assuming an incomplete search was exhaustive. A prompt-level repair is cheap and preserves working behavior, unlike prior rejected mechanisms that added automatic verification hooks or output compaction. Likely benefit: fewer confident but incorrect completions on exact-reconstruction tasks. Likely regression: the model may spend extra steps gathering stronger evidence before editing, but this should be limited because the change adds guidance only and no automatic commands. This differs from prior attempts because it does not auto-run tests, change truncation behavior, or append runtime warnings; it changes the model’s decision rule from 'plausible synthesis is acceptable' to 'exact-output tasks require authoritative derivation and exhaustive local evidence.'
proposal.hypothesis: If the agent is explicitly instructed not to guess or manually reconstruct exact outputs when evidence is incomplete—and instead to derive exact content from authoritative local sources, use exhaustive searches/counts when completeness matters, and treat each shell call as stateless—it will reduce wrong-output failures caused by plausible but incorrect manual edits or guessed recovered values.
proposal.change_summary: Tighten the system prompt to discourage guessing: tell the model to derive exact outputs from authoritative local evidence, avoid assuming partial searches are exhaustive, remember each shell call is stateless, and inspect the actual graded artifact before finishing.

proposal.rationale: Observed failures repeatedly relied on incomplete search/listing evidence. In `sanitize-git-repo`, the agent ran broad recursive searches whose captured outputs were truncated three times (`grep ... | head -200`, `find ... | xargs ... | head -200`), then edited only two files and missed at least one additional Hugging Face token; the hidden diff excerpt shows another token remained in the contaminated content. In `extract-elf`, `readelf -S`/`-s` output was truncated (`... [8034 original chars; middle omitted] ...`) before the agent wrote an incorrect extractor, so missing section details were plausibly unavailable in-context. There is counterevidence: truncation alone does not prove the model would have used the full output, and `fix-git` failed without any truncation markers. A prior rejected attempt added a textual warning about partial evidence; this proposal differs by preserving the full raw output automatically in a persistent file with only a short pointer added to context, so it gives recoverable evidence with less prompt bloat than rerunning wide searches or appending verbose warnings. Likely regression: small extra disk I/O and a slightly longer tool message; benefit may be limited if the model ignores the saved path.
proposal.hypothesis: If the agent automatically saves full tool output to a file and appends a compact pointer when a bash result is truncated or the command explicitly slices results (`head`/`tail`/`sed -n`), the model will less often treat partial search/listing evidence as exhaustive and will more often follow up on the complete raw evidence, improving tasks that currently miss required edits or structural details because key matches were hidden.
proposal.change_summary: Preserve full raw output from truncated or explicitly sliced shell commands in persistent log files and append a short note with the saved path, so the model can recover complete evidence without bloating prompt history.
